summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old female was admitted with worsening bilateral leg and hand swelling, shortness of breath, and mild erythema in the right leg, five days after completing IV antibiotics for recurrent cellulitis. She had gained 5 pounds recently and reported decreased urine output with foamy urine. Workup revealed no deep vein thrombosis, normal cardiac enzymes, and a suboptimal echocardiogram showing grossly normal systolic function. Her INR was subtherapeutic at 1.8, so she was bridged with enoxaparin. Due to mild signs of cellulitis, she was started on oral clindamycin. Her dyspnea was attributed to possible obstructive lung disease given her 60-pack-year smoking history, and she was discharged with albuterol and ipratropium inhalers. Lisinopril was reduced to 10 mg daily due to reported hypotension. She improved clinically and was discharged home with follow-up for INR monitoring, stress testing, and pulmonary function tests.
problems: Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
